messages:
Anna (Platform): Quick follow-up to the active/active convo: we need a simple, auditable way for edge proxies to know tenant geo-consent + allowed failover regions. Two options: authoritative stamp in control-plane OR client-supplied hint header. pros/cons?
Ryan (Arch): Control-plane stamp wins imo. Centralized, auditable, easy to revoke. Edge keeps cached copy.
Mike C: Agreed. But we must handle new tenants or migration lag. Suggest header as "best-effort" fallback, but only if tenant config allows it.
Sophia (Legal): +1 control-plane. Client headers are user-supplied and not proof of consent for regulated EU PII. If a tenant is flagged as EU-regulated we must never route outside allowed_regions, even during outages.
Anna (Platform): Operational flow proposal: 1) edge checks local cache for tenant_stamp 2) if miss, call control-plane /tenants/{id}/residency 3) if control-plane has no stamp, and tenant.accepts_client_hints = true, accept X-Resident header as tentative 4) otherwise local-first route and flag for operator.
Ryan (Arch): State-machine sketch:
```
case cached_stamp: serve_by(cached_stamp)
case control_plane.exists: cache_and_serve(cp_stamp)
case tenant.accepts_client_hints && req.header(X-Resident): serve_tentative(req.header)
default: serve_local_first + metric("geo.route.fallback")
```
Mike C: Implementation notes: when serving tentative, add internal header `X-Route-Origin: tentative` and `X-Resident-Decision: header`. Emit metric geo.route.tentative and tag tenant_id, region.
Anna (Platform): TTL: default 5m for caches so rollouts can flip quickly. But per-tenant override required. For regulated tenants TTL=0 (no caching) unless ops explicitly set an emergency override.
Sophia (Legal): Make sure TTL semantics are auditable in logs. Also retention of routing decisions must comply with contracts; I'll list retention windows per customer and send to infra.
Ryan (Arch): Edge should keep logic minimal: LRU cache with per-tenant meta {allowed_regions, ttl, accept_client_hints}. Expose a sync endpoint for bulk prewarm. Use JWT signed requests to control-plane.
Mike C: Failover rules: control-plane provides allowed_regions array. Edge only failovers within that list. For tenants without allowed_regions set, fall back to global policy (soft allow cross-region).
Anna (Platform): We also need a per-request header for downstream auditing: `X-Resident-Served-From` with region id, and `X-Route-Origin` (authoritative|tentative|local-first). That helps debugging and later billing.
Sophia (Legal): Please make sure any header that exposes residency is internal-only (strip before returning to customers). Can't leak routing hints to end-users.
infra-bot: Runbook: https://playbook.redwood.local/geo-routing and dashboards: grafana/redwood/geo-routing-now. Ops play: operator_override -> set tenant.ttl=0 and allowed_regions=[...]
Ryan (Arch): Action items: I'll PR edge state-machine + cache impl + tests. Mike to add the header names to internal header doc and metrics, and implement tentative metrics. Anna to add controller API schema for tenant residency (stamp, allowed_regions, accept_client_hints, ttl). Sophia to confirm final retention windows.
Mike C: I'll also add an incident probe that fails canary if more than X tentative routes in 10m for any EU-regulated tenant.
Anna (Platform): Sounds good. If no objections, we'll roll the edge change to canary next week and gate by the metric probes. :thumbsup:
